Yes, one big one. A team note in project memory flags it, and the code matches what the note says.

**`finalize()` is not idempotent** (`src/billing/invoices.py:21`). It POSTs to the external ledger with no idempotency key, so calling it twice records the invoice twice in the ledger. Don't wrap it in retries. Call `finalize_once()` (`src/billing/invoices.py:29`), which skips the POST if `invoice.ledger_ref` is already set.

From reading the code, `finalize_once()` still leaves some gaps:

- **Lost responses still cause duplicates.** `ledger_ref` is only set after a successful response. If the POST reaches the ledger but times out (10s) or errors on the way back, `ledger_ref` stays empty and a second call posts again. Real protection needs an idempotency key, for example the invoice ID, if the ledger API supports one.
- **The check only looks at the object in memory.** Nothing in this file writes `ledger_ref` to the database (the column comes from `migrations/0003_add_ledger_ref.sql`). If the caller doesn't save the invoice after finalizing, a freshly loaded copy will look unfinalized.
- **Concurrent calls aren't protected.** Two workers finalizing the same invoice at once can both see `ledger_ref` empty and both post. Nothing locks against that.
- **The amount isn't validated.** It's just `subtotal_cents + tax_cents`, so tax has to be computed before you finalize.
- **There are no tests or callers in this repo**, so nothing will catch a regression. Callers presumably live elsewhere, so check those before changing either function's signature or behavior.

If you're changing this code, adding an idempotency key on the ledger POST would fix the first and third gaps at the source.
